title: Model rollout: regional GPU & KV cache impact (snapshot)
content:
Purpose:
Quick-turn planning sheet to estimate incremental GPU needs and KV cache impact across regions for the staged rollout of model-v2.1 (dense 8-bit variant + KV-prefix caching enabled). This is a working spreadsheet snapshot used to drive canary scheduling and capacity purchases.

High-level summary:
- Expected global QPS increase (p95 requests/hour) after rollout: +28% baseline for text-generation endpoints that adopt v2.1 as primary variant.
- KV cache footprint per active session grows by ~65% due to longer context windows and richer priming; this increases per-GPU memory pressure and effective concurrent sessions.
- Immediate near-term incremental GPU need (4-week horizon): +14 A100s distributed across three regions (us-west1, europe-west1, ap-southeast1) under current traffic routing policy.
- Risk: regional hotspot in europe-west1 if canary weight >20% before cache eviction policy tuned.

Key assumptions (editable):
- Baseline model in prod: v2.0 (int8 compatible), average tokens per request: 120, avg latency per token: 7.4ms on A100 (16G), KV cache hit rate baseline: 18%.
- New model v2.1: avg tokens per request: 145, infer token latency on A100 (16G): 9.1ms, estimated KV per-session footprint: 1.65x of v2.0.
- Traffic ramp plan: week0 canary 5%, week1 15%, week2 40%, week3 70%, week4 100% (final).
- Autoscaling behaviours unchanged; we model minimum reserve ratios to meet 99th percentile latency SLO.

CSV table: region, current-A100s, baseline-concurrent-sessions, expected-concurrent-sessions-v2.1, incremental-A100s-required, kv-cache-total-GB
us-west1, 42, 1200, 1450, 4, 780
europe-west1, 28, 820, 1035, 6, 610
ap-southeast1, 12, 360, 440, 4, 260
us-east4, 18, 520, 665, 0, 340

Notes on the table: incremental A100s are conservative and assume shard packing efficiency of 72% (we lose some packing due to larger KV memory allocations). europe-west1 shows the largest incremental need due to both higher ramp and lower spare capacity. us-east4 shows 0 incremental GPUs because there are available burst slots and a healthy KV eviction TTL tuned for that region.

KV cache footprint details (sample calculation):
- avg KV entries per session (v2.0): 42 entries, avg entry size (serialized): 1.2KB -> 50.4KB per session baseline.
- v2.1 increases avg entries to ~66 and avg serialized size to 1.9KB -> 125.4KB per session.
- Multiply by active concurrent sessions in region -> region-level KV memory shown in table (rounded).

Simulation results (micro-sim with 1-minute timestep, 7-day trace seed):
- With rollout schedule above and current eviction policy (TTL 30m, LRU), europe-west1 KV utilization exceeds soft threshold (75% of aggregate GPU VRAM reserved for cache) by day 11 of the rollout ramp; p99 tail latency degrades by 18% if no corrective steps taken.
- If we apply aggressive shard consolidation (pack factor +5%) + lower batch size on europe-west1 for 48h during peak ramp, the simulator predicts we avoid allocating 2 extra A100s while keeping p99 within 5% of SLO.

Operational mitigations and runbook snippets:
- Short-term (immediate): hold canary at 15% in europe-west1 until eviction TTL reduced to 22m and cache fields compacted (see linked artifacts for compaction script).
- Mid-term (1–2 weeks): schedule 6 extra A100s reservation for europe-west1 with auto-burst off; enable prioritized routing to us-west1 for non-enterprise customers to reduce europe-west1 pressure.
- Long-term (3+ weeks): implement adaptive KV eviction (LRU with token-age weighting) and trial quantized-kv-storage (4-bit packed) to reduce per-entry size by ~30%.

Open questions / items to resolve:
- Confirm sustained qps growth assumptions from Product (growth vs feature adoption) - product owner ticket: JIRA-ENGINF-987.
- Confirm whether enterprise tenants should be pinned to dedicated pools during rollout (affects surge capacity).
- Validate kernel-level memory overheads on A100 80GB vs 40GB for quantized-kv-storage experiment.

Action checklist (owner tags):
- Priya D: run targeted micro-sims for europe-west1 using the most recent 72h traffic slice (due 2026-01-14).
- Diego A: prepare reservation quote for additional 14-day capacity buffer in europe-west1 (due 2026-01-18).
- Maya C: merge compaction script and schedule canary hold gating (due 2025-11-27).

Appendix: quick sensitivity matrix (delta GPUs if key variables shift)
- +10% avg tokens per request -> +3 A100s global (concentrated in regions with high session length).
- KV per-session footprint +20% -> +5 A100s (europe-west1 heavy).
- Pack efficiency drop from 72% -> 65% -> +6 A100s immediate.

Bottom line (one-liner): hold europe-west1 canary at <=15% until KV eviction compaction and packing optimizations are in place; reserve 6 A100s for europe-west1 as insurance and target 4 extra A100s for global burst capacity in week2.
